reasoning_trace.description: MANDATORY: You MUST describe what you see in the images (Charts, System Models) to prove you have analyzed them.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures and charts that illustrate the proposed SMART network architecture, experimental setup, and results. Figure 1 shows the SMART network architecture, which includes a submarine cable with multiple sensing joints and shore-based transceivers. Figure 2 depicts the experimental setup, which consists of a two-span single-mode fiber link with a sensing joint at the optical in-line amplification position. Figure 3 shows the synthesized RTL logic schematic for frequency modulation of the sensed temperature. Figure 4 illustrates the modulation and multiplexing of sensing information, including the electrical spectrum of the frequency-modulated waveform and the optical spectrum of the sensing waveform and ISAC waveform. Figure 5 shows the Q factors of 100 km transmitted DP-QAM16 signals under different launched optical powers. Figure 6 illustrates the impact of optical SSB modulation frequency on ISAC performance, including Q factors and the maximum visible harmonic wave order. Figure 7 shows the measured frequency difference between the imaged harmonic waves at the mixer RF output with frequency-modulated sensing information. Figure 8 depicts the measured relative frequency against DFT length using different orders of harmonic waves generated by sensing information. Figure 9 shows the error bars of the sensed temperature at different DFT lengths, by analyzing different-order harmonic waves. Figure 10 illustrates the error bar curves of temperature estimation using the FPGA-programmed temperature-to-frequency LUT implemented at the sensing joint.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed SMART network uses a dense and compatible ISAC scheme, which enables the co-transmissions of communication signals and sensing information. The ISAC scheme is based on digital subcarrier modulation (DSCM) and frequency modulation of sensing information. The frequency blanks of DSCM can be used to allocate sensing information, achieving dense ISAC. The system uses a joint electrical frequency modulation (FM) and optical single-sideband (SSB) modulation to flexibly tune the allocated frequency of sensing signals, realizing the dense and low-interference ISAC. The sensing information is modulated onto the frequency-modulated sensing signals, which are then coupled into the optical ISAC signal. The system uses a space-time coded DSCM signaling process to balance the signal quality across subcarriers. The system also uses a compatible DSP to demodulate the sensing information, which is based on the frequency estimation approach.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports several metrics, including the Q factors of 100 km transmitted DP-QAM16 signals, the maximum visible harmonic wave order, and the error bars of the sensed temperature. The reported metrics are physically consistent and align with the proposed system mechanism and ISAC coupling mode. The Q factors are reported to be around 8.5-9.5 dB, which is a reasonable value for a 100 km transmission link. The maximum visible harmonic wave order is reported to be up to 11, which is a high value that indicates the system's ability to accurately demodulate the sensing information. The error bars of the sensed temperature are reported to be around 0.0625°C, which is a reasonable value for a temperature sensing system.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed SMART network solves several problems, including the need for a dense and compatible ISAC scheme, the need for a system that can accurately demodulate sensing information, and the need for a system that can balance signal quality across subcarriers. However, there are still some open challenges, including the need for further improvement in the system's performance, the need for a more detailed analysis of the system's complexity and power consumption, and the need for a more comprehensive evaluation of the system's scalability and flexibility.
